_comment: BAND-SPLIT. Band-local clusters for band1_lower_meadows. `order` is this entry's index in the merged array and is the ONLY thing that decides merge position -- never file order, never band order. Existing entries keep the index they had before the split because the merged array order is the order props are added to the scene tree, and Godot silently auto-renames same-named siblings by that order. A new entry in this band takes an unused order in this band's reserved range 1000-1999, which no other band can collide with; do not renumber an existing one.

props._why: the cluster's anchor -- an anvil mounted on its own stump
faces the anvil across the nook -- pulled in 0.7m (round 1 blind critic: the anvil/whetstone and crate/workbench read as two separate groups, not one station)
a sharpening stone within reach of the bench -- pulled in 0.4m, same reason
stock crate behind the anvil -- pulled in 0.9m, same reason
a tool left leaning, mid-repair -- pulled in 0.3m, same reason
the cluster's anchor -- overflow from the last harvest

set right against the barrel's side, not just nearby -- round 2 blind critic: a loose arc of props near a wall reads as dumped, not a task. This is meant to read as one pile: a load just carried out and set down together.

touching the barrel's other side, tipped at an angle rather than square -- just set down, not arranged. FarmCrate_Carrot swapped out earlier (round 1 blind critic): its vertex-colour-tinted contents render as an unreadable white/grey smear, a model defect not a placement one.
in front of the pile, facing back toward it -- the tool that did the carrying, set down after
the big piece of the same load, closing the pile from the front

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor -- a travelling trainer's pack, dropped beside the practice-meadow path, kept as its own separate stop rather than crammed against the supply pile (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'reads as three container props at even spacing... scatter-list output, not a place'). Sited off route 2 ([18,-24]->[30,-40], terrain_playground.json), inside the practice-meadow clearing (vegetation.json, centre [30,-40] r16) but well short of the arena itself.

EV7-clusters-fix: the pile's anchor. This meadow slopes here for real -- a corner-height probe against the crate's own exact footprint (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd) measures 0.137-0.172m of spread across the headings tried, barely moved by yaw alone (165deg: 0.137m vs the old -25deg heading's 0.145m -- yaw was never going to fix this on its own). `sink_m` 0.08 is what actually settles it: added to the model's own ~0.05m embed, the crate's rigid bottom sits ~0.13m below the sampled centre height, which is deeper than half this footprint's worst-case corner spread, so every corner ends up buried in the terrain mesh rather than floating above it, regardless of which way it's turned. `Bench` (a trestle table) is DROPPED entirely -- the critic's own offered alternative ('drop the table and commit to a supply cache at a waypoint composition'): props.gd places every prop flush to the ground with no way to rest one ON another, so the table's flat top could never actually hold the crate/sack/barrel it was meant to -- they always passed clean through its legs. A cache of things set down together, not a furnished stop, is what this system can honestly build.

EV7-clusters-fix: touching the crate's side (0.83m centre-to-centre, matching the two footprints' combined radius) so the pair reads as one pile someone set down together, not a scatter -- distinct spacing from the pack 1.9m away, breaking the old even 3-way spacing the critic named as 'placed by script.' Still the plain supply barrel, not the farmhouse's apple-branded one.

EV7-clusters-fix: the cluster's anchor, moved to hug the footbridge's own west landing (tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd -- bridge local frame x=-5.3, z=1.4, just outside the deck/rail collider's z=+/-1.05 half-extent and past the stone abutment tile at local x=-3.9..-5.9) instead of sitting marooned in open lawn ~3m further out (a genuine blind critic on the shipped state: 'marooned ~6m from the house and ~4m off the bridge head in open lawn'). `sink_m` buries the crate's own shallow 0.05m embed a little further so grass doesn't show lit up under its skirt -- this spot is flat (0.000-0.006m corner spread, real terrain data, not sloped), so the old 'floating crate' complaint here was the shallow embed, not a slope.

EV7-clusters-fix: actually leaning against the crate's near face now, not standing bolt upright ('the axe LEVITATES: bolt upright, unsupported, haft ending mid-air'). This model is authored vertical in its own glTF (a baked -90deg node rotation puts its long axis on Y regardless of yaw -- confirmed with tools/_probe_ev7fix.gd, not guessed), so no yaw value could ever lay it down; `pitch_deg` is new on scripts/world/props.gd for exactly this. Anchor and pitch picked from the same probe's world-space AABB check so the tilted mesh's low end sits in the grass and its body actually overlaps the crate's east face (~0.05m real contact, not just visually adjacent), clear of the crate's own footprint so it doesn't clip through a corner.

EV7-clusters-fix: moved to the crate's own east/bridge-facing side, in front rather than tucked behind it ('the rope coil -- the most purpose-carrying prop -- is 90% hidden behind the crate'). This is the side a player sees first walking off the bridge, so the repair stock reads immediately instead of needing to walk around the crate to find it.

EV7-clusters-fix: water bucket at the pile's far (west) side, foot of the pile -- kept off the deck/rail collider the same way the rest of the cluster is now (local z 1.75, not 0.89 like the position this replaced, which was inside the walkway's own collider footprint).

BAND1-D1-v2, GATE-D coordinator directive: the camp's actual focus. quaternius_survival's Bonfire (logs, unlit -- Bonfire_Fire's extra surface shares the same combined mesh with the logs rather than isolating a flame, checked before use) plus `glow:"campfire"` (scripts/world/campfire_glow.gd, new) for the light/flame-billboard/ember/smoke overlay: the critic's central finding was that the single most important prop for the word 'camp' was absent from a build that already ships it. Everything else in this cluster is arranged around this point, not spaced along a line beside it.

Long seat facing the fire across it -- length axis roughly tangent to the fire so two people could sit side by side and both face in. 2.78m long (measured, tools' own probe pattern), so kept a full 2m+ from the fire ring rather than crowding it.

A second, smaller seat on the opposite side of the fire from the bench -- not a second copy of the same prop, so the ring reads as people sitting at different points around one fire rather than one prop repeated.
A third, informal seat -- a felled log rolled up to the fire rather than furniture, breaking the bench/stool's own regularity. environment/nature's log_large.glb, not the fantasy-kit crate family.
A smaller loose log at the fire's far side, tilted slightly (pitch) rather than dead level -- one more break from every prop standing perfectly axis-upright, which the critique named directly.
Supply crate touching the bench's near end -- the pile a traveller who stopped here actually lives out of, not a separate cache off to the side.

Leaning against the crate, not centred alone -- the same 'pile someone set down together' composition the existing trainer_camp/bridge_repair_site clusters already use, now built around the fire instead of instead of it.

A second, different-shaped pack near the log seat -- quaternius_survival's Backpack (a different silhouette from the fantasy kit's Bag) so the fire has gear on both sides rather than one prop family repeated around it. Scaled 0.55: measured raw AABB is 3.34x3.12x1.75m, a hiking-pack mesh authored at a scale this pack's other props are not -- unscaled it would dwarf the bench.
Coiled beside the crate/bag pile, the same role it plays at the bridge_repair_site cluster -- a coil of cordage a camp plausibly has.

Water barrel, kept at the outer edge of the ring rather than in the direct sightline to the fire. Measured raw AABB (tools/_probe pattern): 0.698 x 0.898 x 0.698m at scale 1.0 -- already the ~0.9m the coordinator's critique asked for; the v1 frame's '1.7-2m' read was this same barrel photographed close and low against the Bag prop it sat beside, not a wrong scale value. Left at scale 1.0 rather than shrunk further, which would make it wrong twice.

First of four RockPath stones laid as stepping points from the spine's own (360,910) bend toward the fire -- the closest this system can build to the coordinator's 'worn dirt patch' without touching terrain_playground.json's path system, which is outside every Gate-D lane's reach (GATE_D_LANE_CONTRACT section 3). A prop-level worn approach, not a texture one.
Second stepping stone, closer to the fire ring.
Third stepping stone, at the ring's own outer edge.

Fourth stone, off to the side of the direct line from the other three -- an approach reads as worn ground, not a single-file row of identical props, which the critique's own complaint about the rock/wagon/barrel line was exactly about.
